title: review: E8: Jev shadow triage of decision points — log what Jev would decide before any Planner launch, no behaviour change
spec:
Every decision-point Planner launch (planner_runs.py, D3) is a full headless Fable session. Before spending one, record what a typed Jev decision would have been, so we can measure agreement over a week and later let the daemon skip launches Jev is confident about. Build on E2 (T-0214) and P5 (T-0206). Shadow mode only: nothing in the launch path changes.
1. orchestrator/planner_runs.py run(): right after the claim and before launch_planner, call jev_triage(kind, task) (fail-open, 3 s cap) and store its result on the ledger row as jev = {choice, probabilities, confidence, latency_ms} or None.
2. jev_triage(kind, task): state = {kind, task title, spec first 1500 chars, hold_reason, latest review comments (path:line + severity + first 200 chars of issue, max 10), depends_on statuses, attempts}; question 'next_action' of type choice with options fix_round ('write a fix-round task from the review comments'), respec ('the spec itself is wrong; recreate the task'), escalate ('a human must decide: auth, billing, data deletion, or three failed rounds'), noop ('the hold is stale or already superseded; nothing to do'). For kind scouts_done: options synthesize_now / wait_for_more / drop_low_confidence.
3. reconcile()/records: when the launched Planner finishes, compare its observable outcome (a fix-round task created -> fix_round; task superseded -> respec; status blocked or escalation note -> escalate; nothing -> noop) and store agreement = true|false|None on the row.
4. `orchestrator scorecard --by goal` is out of scope here; instead planner_runs.py gains summary() returning {decisions, jev_scored, agreement_rate, mean_confidence} printed by `orchestrator planner-runs --summary` (cli.py).
Tests in tests/test_planner_runs.py with jev.ask monkeypatched: ledger row carries jev; None keeps the row valid; agreement computed for each outcome mapping; summary numbers.
acceptance: `uv run orchestrator planner-runs --summary` prints decisions, jev_scored and agreement_rate on an empty ledger without error
No test asserting launch behaviour changes; launch_planner call count unchanged in existing tests

comments.issue: _safe_jev_triage() runs before the guards in run()'s try block (_session_attached, pool headroom, _SAFE_KEY), so it fires a real Jev HTTP call on every path that never launches a Planner and then discards the result (skip records store no jev). Per _record_skip's own docstring a skip does not block the next tick's retry, so with an interactive Planner attached every daemon tick re-calls run() for the same decision and burns another Jev request against [jev].daily_budget_tokens, adding up to 3s (jev.ask retries once with 0.5s backoff on 429/529 and applies timeout_s per attempt, so ~6.5s worst case, not the 3s cap the docstring claims) to the tick for zero recorded value. Move the call to just before _record_running(), after the guards.

_record_running() sets jev= on retry but never resets r["agreement"], and reconcile()'s claim that scoring happens "once ... never revisited" is wrong: an exited_early record is re-run and re-enters the running branch. A row scored agreement=True on attempt 1 whose retry gets jev_result=None keeps agreement=True with jev=None, so summary() counts it in the agreement_rate denominator while excluding it from jev_scored — the rate is then computed partly over rows that had no shadow choice.

jev_triage() only guards key presence (KeyError/TypeError on access), not value types, so a malformed response with "confidence": null is stored as-is; summary() then does sum(r["jev"]["confidence"] ...) and `orchestrator planner-runs --summary` dies with TypeError on a non-numeric confidence, breaking the CLI on external data in a module whose stated posture is fail-open everywhere.

`orchestrator planner-runs` without --summary falls through both branches and prints nothing while exiting 0, which reads as an empty ledger rather than a missing flag. Either make --summary the default output or error on no subflag.
